response.query: How should operator-in-the-loop studies, rollout/rollback plans, and human-factors measurements be designed for LLM-based automation to measure trust, safety, and usability?
response.answer: Operator-in-the-loop studies should involve iterative testing and feedback loops. Rollout/rollback plans must include clear safety protocols and rapid response strategies. Human-factors measurements should focus on trust and usability through direct user surveys and observational studies.

results.title: Memory in Large Language Models: Mechanisms, Evaluation and ...
results.content: On this basis, we propose a four-way taxonomy (parametric, contextual, external, and procedural/episodic) and a "memory quadruple" (storage location—persistence—write/access path—controllability), and connect mechanism, evaluation, and governance through a causal chain of "write—read—inhibit/update." To avoid distorted comparisons arising from heterogeneous settings, we provide a three-setting parallel protocol (parameter-only, offline retrieval, online retrieval) that decouples model capability from information availability on the same data slice and timeline; we then construct a layered evaluation: parametric memory (closed-book recall, edit differential, memorization/privacy risks), contextual memory (position–performance curves and the "mid-sequence drop"), external memory (decoupling correctness from snippet-level attribution/faithfulness), and procedural/episodic memory (cross-session consistency and timeline replay, E-MARS+). *K*eywords LLM memory; parametric memory; contextual memory; external memory; procedural/episodic memory; three-regime evaluation protocol; passage-level evidence attribution and faithfulness; long-context; knowledge editing and unlearning; temporal governance and auditing.

results.title: Track: San Diego Poster Session 4 - NeurIPS 2026
results.content: ##### **MuRating: A High Quality Data Selecting Approach to Multilingual Large Language Model Pretraining**. Data quality is a critical driver of large language model performance, yet existing model-based selection methods focus almost exclusively on English, neglecting other languages that are essential in the training mix for multilingual LLMs. We introduce MuRating, a scalable framework that transfers high-quality English data-quality signals into a multilingual autorater, capable of handling 17 languages. Deep networks have shown remarkable performance across a wide range of tasks, yet getting a global concept-level understanding of how they function remains a key challenge. In this work, we put emphasis on the faithfulness of such concept-based explanations and propose a new model with model-inherent mechanistic concept-explanations. We also leverage foundation models to propose a new concept-consistency metric, C$^2$-Score, that can be used to evaluate concept-based methods. Our objective is to reveal the concepts encoded in CLIP embeddings by learning a surrogate representation, which is expressed as a linear combination of human-understandable concepts evident in the image.
